metadata.versions: PurrNet 1.23.0-beta.40 · FishNet 4.7.3 · Mirror 96.0.1 · NGO 2.13.2 · Fusion 2.1.2 Stable 2279
metadata.note: One published run. CPU stability observation supplied separately by the benchmark operator. Selected categories, no overall ranking.

charts.takeaway: PurrNet used 34% less downstream bandwidth than FishNet across the state replication tests.
charts.figure_method: Mean of three transform and synced-variable workloads. 100 objects, 10 s windows. On-wire server downstream.
charts.figure_caveat: Single run; variability not measured. Fusion used Photon relay; replication behavior differs between netcodes.
charts.chart_subtitle: Server downstream, MiB/s, lower is better
charts.chart_note: * NGO completed all 3 tests with server overload.
charts.method: Arithmetic mean: MoveY, MoveWander, SyncVars. 100 objects · 10 s per test · on-wire server downstream · 1 MiB = 1,048,576 bytes.
charts.caveat: One benchmark run; no repeat variability measured. Native replication behavior differs. Fusion uses Photon relay. Full methodology at the link below.
charts.alt: State replication bandwidth. PurrNet used 34% less downstream bandwidth than FishNet across the state replication tests. NetworkTransform + SyncVars, 100 connections, 20 Hz.

charts.kicker: RPCs: server broadcasts + client inputs, 100 connections, 20 Hz
charts.takeaway: PurrNet used 53% less server CPU than Mirror and 24% less than FishNet in the messaging tests.
charts.figure_method: Mean of two RPC workloads: server broadcasts + client inputs. 10 s windows. Whole-process CPU, no idle subtraction.
charts.figure_caveat: Benchmark + OS only. Observed CPU variation around ±1% (operator measurements). Fusion used Photon relay.
charts.chart_subtitle: Whole-process CPU, % of one core, lower is better
charts.chart_note: * NGO completed both workloads; server-broadcast RPCs were overloaded.
charts.method: Arithmetic mean: SendRPC and ClientInput. 100 connections · 20 Hz · 10 s per test · CPU includes all process threads, with no idle subtraction.
charts.caveat: The benchmark operator reports CPU variation of around ±1% on a server running only the benchmark and OS. This is a separate operator observation, not a per-netcode error bound calculated from this snapshot. Same Ryzen 5 3600 server; 60 fps cap. Fusion uses Photon relay.
charts.alt: Messaging server CPU. PurrNet used 53% less server CPU than Mirror and 24% less than FishNet in the messaging tests. RPCs: server broadcasts + client inputs, 100 connections, 20 Hz.

charts.kicker: NetworkTransform + SyncVars + RPCs + spawn/despawn, 100 connections, 20 Hz
charts.takeaway: PurrNet’s estimated GC allocation rate was 69% lower than FishNet’s across the active workloads.
charts.figure_method: Mean allocation rate across six active workloads, 10 s windows. Idle connections and static objects excluded.
charts.figure_caveat: Estimated from positive managed-heap growth between frames. Single run; variability not measured.
charts.chart_subtitle: Estimated server GC allocation, KiB/s, lower is better
charts.chart_note: * NGO completed all six workloads; 4 were overloaded.
charts.method: Arithmetic mean of server gcAllocBytesPerSec across MoveY, MoveWander, SyncVars, SendRPC, ClientInput and SpawnChurn at 100 connections and 20 Hz. 10 s windows; Idle and Static excluded. 1 KiB = 1,024 bytes.
charts.caveat: Allocation is estimated from positive managed-heap growth between frames, not a precise allocation count. NGO includes overloaded workloads and is not eligible for a best-value claim. One run; no repeat variability measured.
charts.alt: GC allocation across workloads. PurrNet’s estimated GC allocation rate was 69% lower than FishNet’s across the active workloads. NetworkTransform + SyncVars + RPCs + spawn/despawn, 100 connections, 20 Hz.

charts.kicker: NetworkTransform + SyncVars + RPCs + spawn/despawn, 10 → 100 connections, 20 Hz
charts.takeaway: PurrNet used 27% less additional downstream bandwidth per connection than FishNet, from 10 to 100 connections.
charts.figure_method: Average added bandwidth: (downstream at 100 connections − at 10) / 90 across six active workloads. 10 s windows.
charts.figure_caveat: Observed cost over this interval, not a projection. Single run; variability not measured. Fusion used Photon relay.
charts.chart_subtitle: Added server downstream, KiB/s per connection, lower is better
charts.chart_note: * NGO completed both suites; the 100-connection suite includes overload.
charts.method: Mean across six load tests of (server downstream at 100 connections − at 10) / 90, at 20 Hz. 1 KiB = 1,024 bytes.
charts.caveat: Observed marginal cost over this interval; not a per-player total or a projection. One run; no repeat variability measured. Fusion uses Photon relay.
charts.alt: Bandwidth per added connection. PurrNet used 27% less additional downstream bandwidth per connection than FishNet, from 10 to 100 connections. NetworkTransform + SyncVars + RPCs + spawn/despawn, 10 → 100 connections, 20 Hz.
